subject: Recap: Prioritizing inference economics + pilot next steps
body:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@cedarbank.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Prioritizing inference economics + pilot next steps

Liam — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and a concise set of next steps.

TL;DR: CedarBank is seeing good product-market fit for the conversational fraud-triage assistant but token costs at peak are the gating factor. We discussed a focused pilot that combines batching + prefix/KV caching and a small cost/latency tradeoff (light quantization) to fit within a constrained pilot budget.

Key pain points we captured:
- Token spend uncertainty: current LLM vendor billing shows token spikes on long multi-turn sessions (~25–40% of spend tied to long conversations).
- Latency sensitivity: product team wants 99th pct latency <200ms for quick triage workflows — heavy batching today is withheld because it sometimes added >150ms tail latency.
- Ops/visibility gaps: no per-route token/latency breakdowns; hard to trace which flows drive cost.
- Procurement budget: pilot budget is roughly $8k/month for third-party inference and infra (CedarBank expects to validate ROI within a 6–8 week window).

Primary goals for the pilot:
1) Demonstrate >=30% reduction in token spend for the fraud-triage flow (via batching + KV caching + prefix trimming).
2) Maintain 99th pct latency under 200ms for interactive sessions.
3) Provide per-route cost/latency dashboards so the product team can make scale decisions.

What we propose (pilot scope):
- 3-week pilot, dedicated Redwood tenant, instrumented route for fraud-triage only.
- Initial optimizations: automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, batching windows tuned for median p99 tradeoff, conservative int8 quantization on candidate model variant.
- Deliverables: weekly token/latency report, dashboard access, a short SOW and cost-projection sheet.
- Ask of CedarBank: sample anonymized usage CSV (tokens per request, session id, latency), and a single procurement contact for contracting.

Requested next steps (please reply inline):
- Confirm pilot budget comfort (target $8k/month).
- Share the usage export we discussed (small sample OK).
- If procurement needs to be looped in, share contact.

Attachments: cedarbank_usage_export.csv (sample), redwood_pilot_onepager.pdf (design).

Thanks — I can put together a one-page SOW once you confirm budget and procurement contact.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Consultant, Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@cedarbank.com>
To: Priyom Das <pri...@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 17:02:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Prioritizing inference economics + pilot next steps

Thanks, Priyom — helpful recap. Confirming a few things from our end:
- Budget: $8k/month is accurate for an initial pilot window. We want to be conservative and show upside.
- Latency: 99th <200ms is a hard ask for the UX team; if batching introduces tail increases we need mitigation plans (e.g., adaptive batching).
- Data/sample: I attached a stripped sample export from our logs (see cedarbank_usage_export.csv). I redacted PII.

Looping Helen Park (procurement) for contracting. Helen — we’d like Redwood to run a 3-week pilot on our fraud-triage route. Priyom will propose SOW and cost projection.

Liam O'Connell
Head of Product, CedarBank
liam.oconnell@cedarbank.com | +1 (617) 555-0124

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@cedarbank.com>, Helen Park <helen.park@cedarbank.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap: Prioritizing inference economics + pilot next steps (CedarBank)

Internal note — forwarding the thread and Liam's sample. Short asks for the deal:
- Can we draft a 3-week pilot SOW that focuses on the fraud-triage route only, with a target cost of ~$6k–8k for the run (we can price two configurations: conservative and aggressive)?
- Technical approach: Vivek, recommend: (1) set up per-route tracing, (2) enable KV caching for session prefixes, (3) implement adaptive batching with a 25ms micro-batching window default and p99-targeted overflow bypass. Also propose light int8 quantization option if quality holds.
- Benchmarks: need an econ sheet showing expected % token savings for typical session length buckets (0–50 tokens, 50–250, 250+).

Marissa — can you own the commercial SOW + the 2-tier price (pilot base + optional telemetry add-on)? I’ll build the technical appendix.

— Priyom

Subject: Redwood pilot SOW & cost sketch — CedarBank fraud-triage

Hi Liam / Helen — following up with a short SOW sketch and a cost outline for the 3-week pilot we discussed. Attached: redwood_pilot_sow_v1.pdf and the sample usage you provided.

Summary of pilot (3 weeks):
- Scope: Fraud-triage route only (instrumented).
- Objectives: >=30% token spend reduction; maintain 99th pct latency <200ms; deliver weekly dashboards and a final ROI write-up.
- Technical levers: KV/prefix caching, adaptive batching (25ms baseline), optional int8 model variant testing.

Cost sketch (illustrative):
- Base pilot: $6,750 (includes reserved inference capacity for the route, telemetry, and 1 integration hour per week).
- Add-on (detailed telemetry & extended retention): +$1,250.
- Total (with add-on): $8,000 (matches your stated constraint).

Deliverables & timeline:
- Week 0 (setup): tenant, route wiring, dashboards.
- Week 1: enable caching + adaptive batching, baseline report.
- Week 2: tuning and token-savings experiments.
- Week 3: final report, ROI calc, handoff notes.

Next steps:
1) Helen — please confirm procurement path and whether a formal PO is needed before start.
2) Liam — confirm acceptance of the $6,750 base (or $8,000 with telemetry) and a target kickoff of Sep 22.
3) We’ll upload an official SOW & DocuSign quote to the HubSpot deal (link below) once procurement confirms.
